## :angry: Not acting on last week's feedback

::: {.nobullets}
* Temporary code like `head()` or `learncrimemapping::check_code()` in script file
* Loading packages part-way through a script
* `read.csv()` etc. instead of `read_csv()`
* Lines (including comments) over 80 characters long
* Not using blank lines to separate chunks of code
* Comments that don't start with `#` _and a space_, e.g. `# This is a comment`
:::

## :warning: Don't use `ggplot()` (yet) to make maps

Instead of this: 

```{r}
#| eval: false

ggplot() +
  annotation_map_tile(type = "cartolight", zoomin = 0, progress = "none") +
  geom_sf(data = thefts_vehicles_sf, colour = "#FF0000", alpha = 0.1) +
  labs(caption = "Map tiles ©️ CARTO; data ©️ OpenStreetMap contributors") +
  theme_void() +
  theme(plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0))
```

::: {.fragment}
You can just use this:

```{r}
#| eval: false

hotspot_map(thefts_vehicles_sf, basemap_type = "cartolight", alpha = 0.1)
```
:::

# Co-ordinate reference systems



--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


## Numbers on their own could mean anything

```{r}
#| echo: false

birkbeck <- tidygeocoder::geo(
  "Chandler House, Wakefield Street, London WC1N 1BL"
) |>
  st_as_sf(coords = c("long", "lat"), crs = "EPSG:4326") |>
  select(geometry)

bbk1 <- birkbeck |>
  df_spatial() |>
  select(x, y) |>
  gt() |>
  fmt_number(decimals = 4) |>
  cols_width(x ~ pct(50), y ~ pct(50)) |>
  tab_options(table.width = pct(100)) |>
  opt_table_font(size = "36px")

bbk1_text <- birkbeck |>
  df_spatial() |>
  select(x, y) |>
  mutate(
    text = str_glue(
      "{number(x, accuracy = 0.0001)}, {number(y, accuracy = 0.0001)}"
    )
  ) |>
  pull("text", 1)

bbk2 <- birkbeck |>
  st_transform("EPSG:27700") |>
  df_spatial() |>
  select(x, y) |>
  gt() |>
  fmt_number(decimals = 0) |>
  cols_width(x ~ pct(50), y ~ pct(50)) |>
  tab_options(table.width = pct(100)) |>
  opt_table_font(size = "36px")

bbk2_text <- birkbeck |>
  st_transform("EPSG:27700") |>
  df_spatial() |>
  select(x, y) |>
  mutate(
    text = str_glue(
      "{number(x, accuracy = 1, big.mark = '')}, ",
      "{number(y, accuracy = 1, big.mark = '')}"
    )
  ) |>
  pull("text", 1)

bbk3 <- tibble(x = 174.2, y = 86.8) |>
  gt() |>
  fmt_number(decimals = 1) |>
  cols_width(x ~ pct(50), y ~ pct(50)) |>
  tab_options(table.width = pct(100)) |>
  opt_table_font(size = "36px")
```

:::

## Co-ordinates are only meaningful if we know what they represent


::: {.bigish-text .fragment .center}
numeric co-ordinates + co-ordinate reference system
:::


:::: {.fragment .bigish-text .top-space}
e.g.

::: {.center}
[`r bbk1_text`]{.inline-box} + [EPSG:4326]{.inline-box}
:::

or

::: {.top-space .center}
[`r bbk2_text`]{.inline-box} + [EPSG:27700]{.inline-box}
:::

::::

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


## Co-ordinate reference systems specify …


:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="25%}
… an origin point
:::

::: {.column width="75%}
e.g. in the British National Grid (EPSG:27700):

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-asp: 0.8

osgb_grid <- read_sf(
  "OS-British-National-Grids/os_bng_grids.gpkg",
  layer = "20km_grid"
)

bounding_box <- birkbeck |>
  st_transform("EPSG:27700") |>
  add_row(geometry = st_sfc(st_point(c(0, 0)), crs = "EPSG:27700")) |>
  st_bbox()

ggplot() +
  annotation_map_tile(type = "cartolight", zoomin = 0, progress = "none") +
  geom_sf(data = st_sfc(st_point(c(0, 0)), crs = "EPSG:27700"), size = 5) +
  geom_sf(data = birkbeck, colour = "blue3", size = 5) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    limits = c(bounding_box$xmin, bounding_box$xmax),
    expand = expansion(add = 50000)
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(bounding_box$ymin, bounding_box$ymax),
    expand = expansion(add = c(100000, 150000))
  ) +
  coord_sf(crs = "EPSG:27700") +
  theme_void()
```
:::

::::


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


## Co-ordinate reference systems specify …


:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="25%}
… an origin point

… a unit of measurement
:::

::: {.column width="75%}
e.g. in the British National Grid (EPSG:27700):

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-asp: 0.8

ggplot() +
  annotation_map_tile(type = "cartolight", zoomin = 0, progress = "none") +
  geom_sf(data = st_sfc(st_point(c(0, 0)), crs = "EPSG:27700"), size = 5) +
  geom_sf(data = birkbeck, colour = "blue3", size = 5) +
  annotate(
    "label",
    x = bounding_box$xmax / 2,
    y = 0,
    label = "distances in metres",
    fill = NA,
    label.size = NA,
    size = 4,
    vjust = 1
  ) +
  annotate(
    "segment",
    x = 6000,
    xend = bounding_box$xmax,
    y = 0,
    yend = 0,
    arrow = arrow(length = unit(12, "pt"), ends = "both", type = "closed"),
    colour = "grey25"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    limits = c(bounding_box$xmin, bounding_box$xmax),
    expand = expansion(add = 50000)
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(bounding_box$ymin, bounding_box$ymax),
    expand = expansion(add = c(100000, 150000))
  ) +
  coord_sf(crs = "EPSG:27700") +
  theme_void()
```
:::

::::


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


## Co-ordinate reference systems specify …


:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="25%}
… an origin point

… a unit of measurement

… a system for representing a spherical earth on a flat map
:::

::: {.column width="75%}
e.g. in the British National Grid (EPSG:27700):

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-asp: 0.8

ggplot() +
  annotation_map_tile(type = "cartolight", zoomin = 0, progress = "none") +
  geom_sf(data = osgb_grid, fill = NA, linetype = "dotted", linewidth = 0.75) +
  geom_sf(data = st_sfc(st_point(c(0, 0)), crs = "EPSG:27700"), size = 5) +
  geom_sf(data = birkbeck, colour = "blue3", size = 5) +
  annotate(
    "label",
    x = bounding_box$xmax / 2,
    y = 0,
    label = "distances in metres",
    fill = NA,
    label.size = NA,
    size = 4,
    vjust = 1
  ) +
  annotate(
    "segment",
    x = 6000,
    xend = bounding_box$xmax,
    y = 0,
    yend = 0,
    arrow = arrow(length = unit(12, "pt"), ends = "both", type = "closed"),
    colour = "grey25"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    limits = c(bounding_box$xmin, bounding_box$xmax),
    expand = expansion(add = 50000)
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(bounding_box$ymin, bounding_box$ymax),
    expand = expansion(add = c(100000, 150000))
  ) +
  coord_sf(crs = "EPSG:27700") +
  theme_void()
```
:::

::::


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


## But that (usually) only works for a part of the world


:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}
EPSG:27700 works for London, UK …

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-asp: 0.8

ggplot() +
  annotation_map_tile(type = "cartolight", zoomin = 0, progress = "none") +
  geom_sf(
    data = st_transform(
      st_as_sf(
        tidygeocoder::geo("London, United Kingdom"),
        coords = c("long", "lat"),
        crs = "EPSG:4326"
      ),
      "EPSG:27700"
    ),
    size = 3
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(add = 10000)) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(add = 10000)) +
  coord_sf(crs = "EPSG:27700") +
  theme_void()
```
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
… but not for Sydney, Australia:

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-asp: 0.8

ggplot() +
  annotation_map_tile(type = "cartolight", zoomin = 0, progress = "none") +
  geom_sf(
    data = st_transform(
      st_as_sf(
        tidygeocoder::geo("Sydney, Australia"),
        coords = c("long", "lat"),
        crs = "EPSG:4326"
      ),
      "EPSG:27700"
    ),
    size = 3
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(add = 10000)) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(add = 10000)) +
  coord_sf(crs = "EPSG:27700") +
  theme_void()
```
:::

::::


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


## An EPSG code represents an entry in a database of co-ordinate systems

For example …

::: {.bigish-text}
```{r}
#| echo: false

crsuggest::crs_sf |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  filter(
    crs_code %in% c("2240", "3603", "6538", "26916", "26967", "27700", "32610")
  ) |>
  arrange(crs_name) |>
  select(crs_code, crs_name, crs_units) |>
  mutate(
    covers = case_match(
      crs_code,
      "2240" ~ "US state of Georgia",
      "3603" ~ "US state of Missouri",
      "6538" ~ "New York City",
      "26916" ~ "Mid-west of North America",
      "26967" ~ "US state of Georgia",
      "27700" ~ "Great Britain",
      "32610" ~ "West coast of North America"
    ),
    crs_code = str_glue("EPSG:{crs_code}"),
    crs_units = case_match(
      crs_units,
      "m" ~ "metres",
      "us-ft" ~ "feet"
    )
  ) |>
  select(crs_name, crs_code, crs_units, covers) |>
  add_row(
    crs_name = "WGS84",
    crs_code = "EPSG:4326",
    crs_units = "degrees",
    covers = "whole world"
  ) |>
  gt() |>
  cols_label(
    crs_name ~ "co-ordinate reference system",
    crs_code ~ "EPSG code",
    crs_units ~ "units",
    covers ~ "area covered"
  ) |>
  cols_align(align = "left")
```
:::

::: {.fragment .top-space}
EPSG:4326 can be used anywhere in the world

_but_ degrees are a difficult unit to work with
:::


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


## Co-ordinates only make sense with the _right_ CRS


:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}
#### :sunglasses: `r bbk1_text` + "EPSG:4326"

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-asp: 1

birkbeck
```

co-ordinates make sense
:::

::: {.column width="50%" .fragment}
#### :astonished: `r bbk1_text` + "EPSG:27700"

```{r}
#| echo: false

st_set_crs(birkbeck, "EPSG:27700")
```
no error message, but co-ordinates don't make sense

:::

::::


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


## Which CRS should I use?

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="33%" .fragment}
#### Spatial file formats

e.g. `.gpkg`, `.geojson`, `.shp`

**R will automatically extract CRS from data file**
:::

::: {.column width="33%" .fragment}
#### Lat/long data

e.g. `.csv` with columns called `latitude`/`longitude` or similar

**Use EPSG:4326**
:::

::: {.column width="33%" .fragment}
#### Other non-spatial file format

e.g. `.csv` with columns called `x`/`y`, etc.

**You _must_ find out which CRS to use**
:::

::::

::: {.fragment .top-space}
**Don't guess**: it will be very hard to work out if you're guess was correct or not
:::

::: {.fragment .top-space}
Ask whoever gave you the dataset
:::
